Personal-data holds — the ones this domain exists to make

A 募集情報等提供事業者 touches two kinds of personal data: the applicant’s (who applied to what) and the protected characteristics an advertisement may not select on. Both are HARD rules here — a human approver cannot override either.

RuleWhat it refusesStatutory groundingExercised in this run
:applicant-consent-missingAn :application/refer without the applicant’s own consent-to-refer flag. The referral record carries an OPAQUE operator-held applicant_ref pointer and no PII payload — the applicant is deliberately not an entity in this public actor’s store, so only a reference travels to cloud-itonami-isic-7810.ADR-2607131000 (this workspace); consent is operator-attested REQUEST input, checked in governor/applicant-consent-missing-violationsyes · HARD hold on the ledger
:ad-content-discriminatoryPublishing or correcting an advertisement whose content relies on a protected characteristic.男女雇用機会均等法5条 · 労働施策総合推進法9条 · Title VII §704(b) · ADEA §4(e) · Equality Act 2010 · AGG §11 (Ausschreibung)yes · HARD hold on the ledger

Approver attribution — measured, register by register

Every row below is a fresh scan of the real store this run produced (each register is walked to arbitrary depth looking for an approver key), not a claim read off the source. In this repo the answer is genuinely MIXED, which is why it is measured: operation’s :request-approval node attaches the approver at [:payload :approved-by], and whether it survives depends on which branch of store/commit-record! handles the effect — only the :assessment/set branch persists payload itself.

RegisterAccessorCommit effectRecordsApprover retained?
jurisdiction assessmentsstore/assessment-ofassessment/set6yes · on record
posting directory (SSoT)store/all-postingsposting/upsert7no · audit only
publication recordsstore/publication-historyposting/mark-published2no · audit only
delisting recordsstore/delisting-historyposting/mark-delisted1no · audit only
correction recordsstore/correction-historyposting/mark-corrected1no · audit only
application referral recordsstore/referral-historyreferral/record1no · audit only
audit ledgerstore/ledger—24no · audit only

This run’s approver(s): op-1. Retained on: jurisdiction assessments — there the approver is real stored data. Not retained on: posting directory (SSoT), publication records, delisting records, correction records, application referral records, audit ledger. For those registers store/commit-record! uses only path (and, for :posting/upsert, value) and never reads payload back out, so the approver never reaches them. Where the Operation dispositions table above reads “approved by” for one of those ops, that name is joined from the run’s own :approval-granted audit fact — audit only — not retained in the record. This page states that plainly rather than printing an approver as though the register held one.

The store’s own append-only ledger carries an :approval-granted fact: no — operation’s :commit node appends only its :committed fact, so the :approval-granted fact carrying :by lives in the run’s in-memory audit channel and in the checkpointer, not in the durable ledger.

Source-republication / database-right basis

A SEPARATE regime from job-advertising accuracy law: whether a third-party source's postings may be republished at all is a database-right / copyright question, independent of whether the posting itself is accurate and lawful. Read straight out of jobsearchops.facts/consent-spec-basis.
